protocol: D-000 new cycle, turn 1 of 3; refute not confirm; PREFERENCE-LADEN D-006-conforming G03/G04 machine-pin and naming act, plus a D-001 MF-6 file-08 edit that flips condition 4 to MET
summary: The mechanics of this entry are the cleanest of any file-08 write I have reviewed. I simulated the five edits against live bytes: every target is unique, the two edits inside the condition-4 row are disjoint, and afterwards the register contains exactly eighteen named identifiers, zero occurrences of PARTLY MET anywhere, and one surviving reserved cell which is G13, the row this entry refuses to name. The condition-4 MET claim also survives its test — D-001 requires named harnesses, owners, and no unevidenced QUALIFIED or DEMONSTRATED, and I verified all three limbs independently, including reading every DEMONSTRATED occurrence in file 08. What fails is the procurability finding. D-006 makes verifying procurability the precondition for this act, and the evidence offered establishes the availability of a hosted CI venue that the entry itself insists is not the representativeness pin.

objections.location: Subject, 'Procurability finding (product sign-off, this date)', read against the macos-x86_64-ref pin
objections.claim: The finding and its evidence are about different objects. The pin is a 2018-class Intel Mac mini with 8 GB; the evidence is that GitHub Actions publishes a hosted native-Intel macOS image, which the entry expressly states is not the representativeness pin.
objections.why: D-006's OBS-T3-02 makes this the gating precondition: 'native Intel Mac hardware is scarcity-exposed — the G03/G04 harness-naming act must verify procurability under its product sign-off, and unprocurability routes through this entry's successor-decision path, never silent Rosetta substitution.' D-094 answers that native Intel Mac hardware 'is procurable for this pin, not unprocurable', and offers one piece of evidence: the `macos-15-intel` hosted image. In the very next bullet the entry says of that label, 'That label is a measurement venue … It is not the representativeness pin.' So on the entry's own characterization the evidence concerns something it has just distinguished from the pinned machine. That a hosted Intel venue exists does not establish that an Apple Mac mini 2018-class unit with Core i5/i7 and 8 GB can be obtained, and no other basis for procurability is asserted. Two features of the draft sharpen rather than soften this. First, the stated venue-allowance test — 'allowed only when the harness records a native Intel CPU brand string and sysctl.proc_translated = 0' — checks architecture and translation but not the pinned model or memory, while a separate sentence requires that 'a venue that does not match the class is rejected at qualification'. A venue can therefore pass the stated allowance test and still fail the class, which means the venue whose existence is offered as procurability evidence may be one the pin excludes. Second, the entry supplies the venue's retirement date itself, August 2027 or Fall 2027, without saying what becomes of the finding if qualification postdates it. If the venue is the intended execution path, the finding is bounded by that date and should say so; if it is not the execution path, it is not evidence for the pin. The gap matters because this precondition is what makes the act D-006-conforming, and the act is what flips condition 4 to MET.
objections.whyNotMustFix: Nothing false is written into file 08 by the five edits — the inserted cells say 'D-006 machine pins recorded', which is true, and claim neither procurability nor QUALIFIED. The anti-substitution discipline is real and stated in three places, including the class-match rejection at qualification, so the failure mode D-006 was guarding against is not opened. And the finding is a product sign-off under the PREFERENCE-LADEN authority D-006 itself carries, so the question is whether the reasoning is recorded honestly, not whether a reviewer would choose the same answer.
objections.repair: State the relation between venue and pin explicitly. Either assert and evidence that the pinned class itself is obtainable, in which case the CI image is context rather than the finding's basis; or make the venue the execution path and pin the class to what that venue actually provides, so the class-match rule cannot reject the only venue offered; or record the finding as venue-bounded, with re-verification or the D-006 successor path triggered at the stated retirement.

whatIVerified: Subject digest at start and end: 263d2565ab8f230d99fd9bba7c631a33c431e6cf0eb7355184afaaac1614db5d, three measurements each, equal to the dispatched value, -r--r--r-- at both ends. Prompt held at bdfa7fd9… across start and end.

The condition-4 MET claim is justified, which I established from D-001's own text rather than from the entry's account. D-001 condition 4 reads 'Required release gates have named harnesses and owners; no document claims `QUALIFIED` or `DEMONSTRATED` without retained evidence.' The requirement is naming, not authoring, so identifiers with no artifact on disk satisfy it — which is also what D-086's adopted projection said in terms, that condition 4 'would still not be MET: two required gates (G03/G04) remain unnamed', naming those two as the sole remaining obstacle.

All three limbs of condition 4 check out. The harness half reaches 18 of 18: file 08 currently holds sixteen 'named: harness.' strings and the two edits add G03 and G04, which I confirmed by simulating the replacements — the result contains exactly eighteen. Owners are unaffected and remain 22 of 22, with G03 and G04 both owned by 'Release engineering'. For the claims half I did not take the entry's 'abstinence' assertion on trust: no gate row's assurance stage asserts QUALIFIED, and all four DEMONSTRATED occurrences in file 08 are safe — a negative staging report 'NOT-RELEASE-QUALIFIED (0/25 demonstrated)', the registry preamble 'All rows are currently below QUALIFIED and DEMONSTRATED', D-001's condition-4 text, and the condition-4 requirement cell itself.

The attack 'presents 16 of 18 after naming, or 18 of 16' fails: the replacement fragment reads '18 of 18 required gates name a recorded identifier', which is eighteen named of the eighteen required — the denominator GHN-V2-B1 established and D-088 wrote.

The attack 'counts reserved v3 identifiers as already named before this act' fails, and the register agrees: the live count of named identifiers is sixteen, G03 and G04 both read 'reserved, not named (D-006 machine pins owed; D-086)', and the entry's rejected alternative records 'zero progress until this act' citing GHN-V1-B2.

The attack 'leaves G03/G04 reserved after claiming they are named' fails, tested by simulation rather than by reading the intent. After applying both gate edits, exactly one 'reserved, not named' string remains in file 08, and it is G13 — the row this entry expressly refuses to name.

All five targets are unique and the two edits that land in the same table row cannot collide. The three fenced targets each occur once and their replacements zero times; '| **PARTLY MET** |' occurs exactly once; 'condition 4 is PARTLY MET' occurs exactly once. Within the condition-4 row the Measured-now fragment occupies offsets 130 to 303 and the standing cell begins at 406, so they are disjoint.

The staleness sweep comes back clean, which for a readiness flip is the check that matters most. '**PARTLY MET**' occurs exactly once in the whole register, and after simulating all five edits the string 'PARTLY MET' appears zero times anywhere in the file. So no second statement is left calling condition 4 partly met while the standing cell says MET.

The attack 'silent Rosetta or Apple-Silicon-hosted Intel' fails on several independent surfaces: the macos-x86_64-ref pin states 'Never Rosetta. Never an Intel userspace on Apple Silicon. Never a translated binary'; the cache-state protocol requires recording 'sysctl.proc_translated' which 'must be 0' on that machine; the venue bullet says 'It is not Rosetta'; and a rejected alternative cites D-006 SF-02 and OBS-T3-02. This matches D-006's own 'native Intel-class hardware, never Rosetta-on-Apple-Silicon'.

The attack 'treats a CI label as the representativeness pin' fails as a matter of the entry's stated position — the label is called a measurement venue and expressly denied pin status, and a rejected alternative repeats it. My objection is the converse of this attack rather than an instance of it: the entry is clear that the label is not the pin, which is exactly why it cannot also serve as the pin's procurability evidence.

The attack 'changes D-006 numeric thresholds' fails: the header refuses it, the pins section is titled 'execute D-006's runner class; do not rewrite it', the procurability section states this is 'not a D-006 successor that drops macOS x86_64 or changes numeric thresholds', and the cache-state protocol preserves D-006's exclusion — 'Analyze RSS and doctor-with-consented-probes RSS remain outside D-006 (unchanged)', which matches D-006's deliberate-silence note.

The pins execute rather than rewrite the D-006 class. D-006 fixes macOS arm64 as 'base-configuration Apple Silicon entry chip (M1-class), 8 GB', macOS x86_64 as native Intel-class, and Linux as '4-vCPU / 8 GB standard cloud-runner class'; the four pins instantiate exactly those with OS families and no threshold movement.

The attacks 'claims QUALIFIED or DEMONSTRATED', 'marks any DR row SATISFIED', 'authorizes docs/v2/implementation/ or flips condition 5' all fail. Both inserted harness cells end 'not authored; not QUALIFIED'; clause 3 states 'MET is not QUALIFIED. MET does not authorize implementation'; clause 5 refuses SATISFIED and the implementation directory; and the rejected alternative 'Flip condition 5. Rejected: C2 is NOT MET; C5 is last' is correct, since D-001 gates condition 5 on conditions 1, 2 and 4 and condition 2 stands at 4 of 30 NOT MET. After this entry conditions 1, 3 and 4 would be MET and condition 2 alone would block condition 5, which the readiness effect states rather than obscures.

The attack 'cited COORD / file 08 / freeze / commit digests do not match' fails: COORD 4ec06988…, file 08 45dc4611… and the freeze all equal live bytes at the start and again at the close; the three commits resolve at full hash to D-086, D-088 and D-093; and D-006's CONSENT digest bfd8a758… is present in COORD.
The attack 'D-093 subjects edited' fails: all three measure the values pinned through that cycle — fd45e7d1…, 1e6a236b… and 856f7cd2… — unchanged.

The attack 'names G03/G04 without a procurability finding' fails in form: a finding exists, is dated, and is attributed to product sign-off. My objection is to what the finding rests on, not to its absence.
The subject terminates with a newline and contains none of the working-note markers. D-094 is absent from COORD, and COORD and file 08 are unmodified in my working tree.
I wrote one file, the verdict named for me, and edited and committed nothing.

objectionNote: I OBJECT with zero MUST-FIX and one SHOULD-FIX. This entry flips a readiness condition, so I tested the flip rather than the prose: I applied all five edits to a copy of the live register and counted the result — eighteen named identifiers, zero survivals of PARTLY MET anywhere in the file, and a single remaining reserved cell which is G13, the row the entry refuses to name. The MET claim itself holds against D-001's actual wording, which asks for named harnesses and owners and an absence of unevidenced claims, and I checked the third limb by reading every DEMONSTRATED occurrence rather than accepting the word abstinence. The objection is narrow and sits at the one place the entry exercises judgment instead of arithmetic. D-006 made procurability the precondition for naming G03 and G04, and the entry's evidence for it is the existence of a hosted Intel runner that the entry, two sentences later, insists is not the representativeness pin. Either that venue can stand in for the pinned 2018-class machine, in which case the class-match rule needs to say so and the pin should describe what the venue provides, or it cannot, in which case its availability is not evidence that the pinned machine is procurable. The draft asserts both halves and never joins them.
